prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. It shows FOUR historical specimen slots of the SAME character labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC; any slot marked UNAVAILABLE is absent evidence. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally. Reconstruct one coherent attested whole form with the original ancient identity; do not combine incompatible variant components, imitate only THX, or substitute a modern Chinese character.

Build genuine smooth stroke trajectories as original harmonious Gothic monoline drawing, with absolutely CONSTANT stroke width around 3% of the full canvas. All strokes must share that width, with round caps and round joins, smooth rounded curves and precise straight bars, no taper, swelling, brush outlines, serifs, pressure modulation, textures or blobs. Keep every required counter and gap clearly open. Essential bar length relationships, branches, descending legs, tiny detached marks and contacts are structural requirements, not decoration.

Use a square 1:1 canvas. Center the ONE glyph inside the central70% with generous clear margins. Output ONLY pure BLACK constant-width strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background, with no labels, text, codepoint, chart, grid, background, frame, shadows, watermark or multiple specimens. Exactly one complete glyph.

Explicit structural/proportion reading aid:
U+3D07B. LEFT separate component is one vertical stem joining THREE horizontal bars; bottom modestly longest, top85–95% bottom, middle slightly shorter. RIGHT compound choose coherent long-sided THX/CCZ whole form after comparing all4. At TOP is a small bent hooked head: an upper-left free tip curves into a rightward top bar, turns down at right and back left into a short neck. A diagonal branch from near its upper-left shoulder extends down-left as another free tip. This head/neck joins a broad OUTER rounded arch; its TWO outside legs descend LONG to baseline, left and right. Immediately under arch top are TWO small shoulder pockets/counters, one each side, made by short inward curved branches from top center to outer sides. INSIDE the broad arch is a SEPARATE upright rounded eye/capsule with exactly TWO interior horizontal dividers, creating THREE stacked white fields. Keep eye separated from arch sides. Eye's center stem extends below it and has ONE short RIGHT-projecting horizontal arm. Beneath that arm the stem meets a longer horizontal starting freely at left, bending RIGHT and DOWN then returning LEFT. A separate small inward hook under it curves right/down into a LONG lower stem crossing the returning outer bend; outer return continues as a free left terminal beyond crossing. Preserve this lower crossed hook course, not a closed box. Three major lower descending ends in chosen THX-type form: outer left leg, inner long tail, outer right leg. Total principal closed fields TWO shoulder pockets plus THREE eye fields; no extra eye divider or fourth eye field.

visual_review.method: white inspection composite compared against all available reference specimens
reading_criteria: Left three-bar stem requires bottom modestly longer than top.
Right long-sided THX/CCZ body: hooked head plus diagonal branch, two shoulder counters and three eye counters.
Eye stem has right arm; lower bent return crossed by inner downward hook with free left terminal.
Outer left/right long legs plus inner lower tail give three major bottom ends.
notes: Native preserves the complete coherent long-sided body, two shoulder pockets, three eye bands and lower crossed return.
Left top and base appear nearly equal rather than clearly longer base; own verdict uncertain pending independent measured proportion check.
caveats: Only potential issue observed is left-bar proportion; preserve all other native courses.
DYC uses shorter shoulder legs; chosen form follows THX/CCZ long legs, not a mixed variant.
